item.title: An Expansion for Taq
item.description: Taq, the taco-based eatery, moved two doors down and more than quadrupled its seating capacity. The post An Expansion for Taq appeared first on Ann Arbor Observer.

item.title: Norma June (Johnson) Crouch
item.description: Affectionately referred to as “Mimi Norm,” she was unwavering in her support of her seven grandchildren. She rarely missed a game or concert, spending countless hours cheering them on. The post Norma June (Johnson) Crouch appeared first on Ann Arbor Observer.

item.title: Townie Homes
item.description: The Zillow listings seem too good to be true: A 2-bed, 2-bath, 800-square-foot house on S. Maple for $125,000. A 3-bed, 3-bath 1,372-square-foot townhome on S. Wagner for $225,000. A 3-bed, 2-bath, 1,232-square-foot home on Jewett for $325,000. The post Townie Homes appeared first on Ann Arbor Observer.

item.title: After the Fall
item.description: Sherrone Moore’s tenure ended in jail. The post After the Fall appeared first on Ann Arbor Observer.

item.title: The Wallenberg House
item.description: “I Spy: the Wallenberg House,” writes first-time entrant Marley Kalt. The post The Wallenberg House appeared first on Ann Arbor Observer.

item.title: Tree Town, a Truck Town?
item.description: “Most people explore the outdoors on four wheels,” says RealTruck’s chief growth officer Tony Ambroza. The post Tree Town, a Truck Town? appeared first on Ann Arbor Observer.

item.title: Syverud Steps Up
item.description: Kent Syverud, chancellor and president of Syracuse University, was unanimously elected by the Board of Regents January 12 as the University of Michigan’s sixteenth president. The post Syverud Steps Up appeared first on Ann Arbor Observer.

item.title: It’s All in the Name
item.description: A new restaurant on S. Main sounds like a not-so-subtle imperative: Eat Thai Ann Arbor. The name was chosen to be simple, but the story of its chef and owner, Teerawat Pho-On, is anything but. The post It’s All in the Name appeared first on Ann Arbor Observer.

item.title: Lisa Brush and Jim Frey
item.description: Brush and Frey fell in love nearly twenty years ago. They first met less than a mile from the Longshore building, while collaborating on Leslie Science & Nature Center’s shift to an independent nonprofit. The post Lisa Brush and Jim Frey appeared first on Ann Arbor Observer.

item.title: Learning in Limbo
item.description: For the first time since 1994, Ann Arbor Public Schools (AAPS) teachers are working with expired contracts. The post Learning in Limbo appeared first on Ann Arbor Observer.
